identity: Civil rights advocate and writer · South Africa · 1946–1977
title: Steve Biko's birth chart
metaDescription: Steve Biko's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.9° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the nine placements whose signs are settled, fixed leads with four. Fixed weight is the scheme’s deep keel: slow to turn, near-impossible to capsize.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 25.9° Sagittarius — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Sun. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Sagittarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 7.0° Sagittarius, Venus was at 19.0° Scorpio, Mars was at 0.7° Capricorn. Read together: a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mercury a third of the circle apart from Saturn, 1.1° off exact. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Venus conjunction Jupiter at 1.2°, and Saturn sextile Neptune at 2.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 7.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Scorpio at 19.0° is in detriment; Mars in Capricorn at 0.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Leo at 8.2° is in detriment. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives fire 4, water 2, air 2, earth 1, and fixed 4, mutable 3, cardinal 2 across the modes. Fire leads with ignition: the first move made early, and certainty arriving ahead of the evidence. Saturn, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Libra into Scorpio during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.2° between one midnight and the next. Which of the two it was depends entirely on the hour, and the hour is not recorded. Rather than pick the likelier half, the reading leaves the Moon open.
